samples.name: 01 · Hello Rect
samples.description: The smallest patch — one shape wired to the Renderer. Start here.

samples.name: 02 · Colour & Fill
samples.description: Colour a shape: a Color node feeds a Fill, and the Fill feeds the Rect.

samples.name: 03 · Animate with Time
samples.description: Move a shape back and forth in a smooth loop, driven by time.

samples.name: 04 · Follow the Mouse
samples.description: A circle follows your mouse pointer.

samples.name: 05 · Slider Control
samples.description: A slider changes the width of a rectangle: the basic interactive control.

samples.name: 06 · Spreads & ForEach
samples.description: Make a list of numbers with Range Spread, then use a ForEach to draw one shape for each.

samples.name: 07 · Grid of Dots
samples.description: A Grid Spread gives one point per cell. Wire it straight into an ellipse to draw an 8×8 grid of dots.

samples.name: 08 · Palette Colours
samples.description: Colour a grid of dots from a four-colour Palette, repeating the colours with Cycle Spread.

samples.name: 09 · Memory (Write → Read)
samples.description: A Write and Read pair remembers a number from one frame to the next. It adds 1 every frame, which turns the hue.

samples.name: 11 · Polar Coordinates
samples.description: A sine and a cosine times a radius give any point on a circle: the basis of every radial layout.

samples.name: 12 · Circle of Shapes
samples.description: Ring Spread and a ForEach place shapes evenly around a circle.

samples.name: 13 · Map: Remap Ranges
samples.description: Map turns one range of numbers into another. Here the mouse’s left-right position sweeps the hue across the rainbow.

samples.name: 14 · Lerp Two Colours
samples.description: Lerp blends one colour into another. A smooth wave of time moves the blend back and forth.

samples.name: 15 · Style Chains
samples.description: Plug one style into another’s base pin to stack fills and strokes on a single shape.

samples.name: 16 · Group + Transform
samples.description: Group joins many layers into one, and Rotate then spins the whole assembly together.

samples.name: 17 · Perlin Noise
samples.description: Perlin noise is smooth randomness: neighbouring inputs give neighbouring results. Here it sets each cell’s height and colour.

samples.name: 18 · Random Spread
samples.description: A random number for each item places 80 ellipses. The same seed always gives the same picture; change the seed to roll again.

samples.name: 19 · If Region (Conditional)
samples.description: An If region runs the nodes inside it only when its condition is true. Here the condition flips with time, so the rect blinks on and off.

samples.name: 20 · Subpatch (Reusable Box)
samples.description: A subpatch wraps part of a patch in a box with its own pins. Double-click to go inside, edit, then climb back out.

samples.name: 21 · Trails (Write*/Read*)
samples.description: Each frame the mouse position is added to a growing list, and the list is drawn as a path: a trail behind the cursor.

samples.name: 22 · Cache Region
samples.description: A Cache region skips its work while its inputs stay the same. Put anything slow inside it.

samples.name: 23 · Polygon from Points
samples.description: A Polygon turns a list of points into one shape, with no ForEach needed.

samples.name: 24 · Path with Tension
samples.description: Raising a Path’s tension turns straight segments into smooth curves. Here time moves it between sharp and smooth.

samples.name: 25 · Spring-follow Mouse
samples.description: A dot follows the mouse as if it were on a spring: it overshoots and settles. Two Write and Read pairs remember its position and speed.

samples.name: 26 · Rasterize (Layer → Image)
samples.description: Rasterize turns a vector layer into a bitmap image, which an Image node then draws back.

samples.name: 27 · Image Sampling Grid
samples.description: Sample Spread reads one colour at each of many points. Here it recolours a 24×24 grid of squares from a picture of a gradient.

samples.name: 28 · Audio-Reactive Visual
samples.description: The loudness of your microphone sets the size of a circle. Allow microphone access when asked.

samples.name: 29 · Oscillator (mouse-pitched)
samples.description: An Oscillator makes a tone and the Output plays it. The mouse’s height sets the pitch, so move the cursor to slide the tone.

samples.name: 30 · Keyboard Branching
samples.description: Press R for a red rectangle or B for a blue ellipse: two If regions each listen for a key.

samples.name: 31 · Vec2 Math
samples.description: Vector Math works on a point as one unit, so you can scale it without splitting it into x and y and joining it again.

samples.name: 32 · Normalize + Polar
samples.description: Vector Math’s normalize turns any direction into one of length 1. Scale it to any length you like.

samples.name: 33 · Gradient Sampling
samples.description: A Gradient blends between colour stops. The mouse’s left-right position picks the colour.

samples.name: 34 · Draw Text
samples.description: Text is drawn like any other shape, with a position, a size and a style.

samples.name: 35 · Wanderer (random drift)
samples.description: A Wanderer gives a point that drifts smoothly over time, for natural-looking movement.

samples.name: 36 · Gaussian Scatter
samples.description: Gaussian places points in a cluster around a centre, thickest in the middle like a bell curve.

samples.name: 37 · Image from URL
samples.description: An ImageURL node downloads a picture and an Image node draws it. Picsum gives a fresh photo for each seed, so this needs an internet connection.

samples.name: 38 · Image Adjust
samples.description: Image filters chain together just like styles: brightness, contrast, saturation and hue.

samples.name: 39 · Pixelate
samples.description: Pixelate shrinks a picture and blows it back up for a chunky, retro look.

samples.name: 40 · Pixel Sort
samples.description: PixelSort reorders runs of pixels by brightness: the classic glitch-art look.

samples.name: 41 · Spread Sort + Shuffle
samples.description: Shuffle a list of numbers, then sort it with Reorder, and watch the result as a bar chart.

samples.name: 42 · Elementary CA
samples.description: A row of on and off cells moves on one step at a time by Wolfram’s rules. Try rules 30, 90 and 110.

samples.name: 43 · Game of Life
samples.description: Conway’s Game of Life, with a Write and Read pair carrying the grid from frame to frame.

samples.name: 44 · Accumulator (Fold)
samples.description: An accumulator passes a running total from one ForEach round to the next. Here it adds up 1 to 10, and every wire still runs left to right.

samples.name: 45 · MIDI CC
samples.description: A MIDI knob (already scaled from 0 to 1) controls the size of a rectangle.

samples.name: 46 · Sound Filter Sweep
samples.description: A Filter on a sawtooth tone. The mouse’s left-right position sweeps the cutoff: a classic synth sound.

samples.name: 47 · ADSR Envelope
samples.description: An Envelope shapes how loud a sound is over time (attack, decay, sustain, release). Press the mouse button to play it.

samples.name: 48 · Pulse Width Drone
samples.description: A Pulse oscillator whose width follows a smooth wave makes a moving tone, and the circle breathes with the loudness.

samples.name: 49 · FFT Spectrum Bars
samples.description: An FFT splits sound into a spectrum, and 128 bars follow your microphone. Allow microphone access when asked.

samples.name: Kinetic Wave
samples.description: A wave of letters travels along rows of text, each row a little behind the last. Every word takes its colour from a palette.

samples.name: Halo
samples.description: A phrase laid around three concentric rings that spin, the inner ones faster. Hue cycles per character and per time for a chromatic chase.

samples.name: The Raven
samples.description: A passage from Poe’s “The Raven” as a serif grid. Each letter fades in and out on its own, in black and white, blurring as it dims.

samples.name: Noise Drift
samples.description: A passage as a monospace grid. Slow noise picks drifting clusters of letters, and inside them the type is pushed around and tinted while the rest stays readable.

samples.name: Type Rain
samples.description: Digital rain: falling characters, every column scrolling at its own speed, and the letters dim as they fall down the canvas.

samples.name: Weight Wave
samples.description: A wave of weight and width rolls through rows of text in a variable font, so every row reflows as its letters get heavier and wider.

samples.name: Spiral Type
samples.description: A phrase scrolls along a spiral and a ring, each letter turning to follow the curve.

samples.name: Glyph Particles
samples.description: Particles are born along the outlines of the letters while the font’s weight swells and shrinks.

samples.name: Write-On Lettering
samples.description: Trim Path writes a word’s outlines one letter after another, with a pen nib riding the drawing end.

samples.name: Kinetic Type
samples.description: Text Animate: letters rise, turn and fade in one after another; a second line rides a rolling sine wave. No ForEach.

samples.name: Fountain
samples.description: The “hello, particles” patch: an emitter sprays particles, gravity pulls them down, drag slows them and wrap-around edges keep them cycling.

samples.name: Text Dust
samples.description: Particles are born inside the letters of a word, so the dust really comes from the letterforms.

samples.name: Attractor Field
samples.description: Turbulence, drag and an attractor shape how the particles move. The attractor also draws a ring that shows how far its pull reaches.

samples.name: Polygon Pinball
samples.description: An octagonal arena that is both drawn and solid: the same shape is shown on screen and used as a wall, so particles bounce off its real edges.

samples.name: Galactic Spiral
samples.description: A swirling force and a pull towards the centre make long, steady spiral arms. Each particle’s trail keeps its own colour, so every strand keeps its hue.

samples.name: Lissajous Threads
samples.description: A 240-dot Lissajous curve. Two sliders pick the X/Y frequency ratio; time drifts the phase.

samples.name: Kaleidoscope
samples.description: A drifting window into a photo, cut to a wedge and repeated as 12 round the centre, every other one mirrored (the Symmetry node in kaleidoscope mode). The window wanders with time.

samples.name: Grid Art
samples.description: A 6×6 grid of little random-walker drawings, each with its own seed: 36 different compositions that share one palette. A slider re-rolls the whole grid.

samples.name: Motion Lab
samples.description: A swaying target followed by Smooth (lags behind), Spring (overshoots and wobbles) and DelayLine (arrives late) in separate lanes against a shared guide, so the differences show at a glance.

samples.name: Eased Stagger
samples.description: A row of dots bobbing in a travelling wave. The ForEach gives each dot its own delay, an Ease curve shapes the bob, and a dot’s place in the row sets its colour.

samples.name: LFO Motion
samples.description: LFOs animating size, colour and position: one LFO with a count of 12 ripples a row of bars, a triangle sweeps the hue, a smooth-random wanders a dot.

samples.name: Phyllotaxis
samples.description: A sunflower spiral: each seed is placed a golden angle round from the last. The colour sweeps from the centre outwards.

samples.name: Smoothed Path
samples.description: A jagged line with a smoothed copy on top: each point is averaged with its left and right neighbours.

samples.name: Grid Ripple
samples.description: A grid of outlined squares rippling outwards from the centre, with colours cycling through a palette across the cells.

samples.name: Curl Flow
samples.description: A grid of streaks that follow a swirling noise field drifting with time: the classic flow-field look.

samples.name: Ripple Field
samples.description: A 25×25 grid of dots pulsing in rings that ripple out from the centre.

samples.name: Noise Wave
samples.description: A 32×32 grid of cells pushed around and recoloured by layered noise that changes with time.

samples.name: Force Field Arrows
samples.description: A 14×14 grid of arrows pointing along a drifting noise field, each with a coloured dot at its tip.

samples.name: Pendulum
samples.description: A classic swinging pendulum that slowly loses energy. Write and Read pairs remember its angle and speed from frame to frame. From The Nature of Code, chapter 3.

samples.name: Wind & Gravity
samples.description: Move the mouse sideways to blow wind while gravity pulls down. Heavier things respond less to the wind, so slide the mass to feel the difference. From The Nature of Code, chapter 2 (forces).

samples.name: Drag
samples.description: A ball falls through thick fluid. Drag pushes against its motion until it stops speeding up and sinks at a steady pace, where gravity and drag balance. From The Nature of Code, chapter 2.

samples.name: Mouse Attraction
samples.description: A mover is pulled towards the mouse by a gravity-like force that grows stronger up close, but is capped and damped so it stays calm. From The Nature of Code, chapter 2.

samples.name: Spring
samples.description: A weight bobs on a spring beneath a hanging point: the spring pulls it back, with gravity and damping. Write and Read pairs remember its position and speed. From The Nature of Code, chapter 3.

samples.name: Seek
samples.description: An agent steers towards a target: it works out which way it wants to go and turns gently towards it, limited by its top speed and steering strength. Two sliders tune it. From The Nature of Code, chapter 5 (autonomous agents).

samples.name: Flow Field
samples.description: A 16×16 grid of arrows pointing along drifting noise. A slider sets how large the swirls are. From The Nature of Code, chapter 5.

samples.name: Shader · Raymarched Gyroid
samples.description: What a single fragment shader can do: a raymarched 3D scene with melting metaballs carved by a gyroid lattice, soft shadows, ambient occlusion, iridescent fresnel and a glowing grid floor. The Scale slider sets the lattice density.

samples.name: Shader · Plasma
samples.description: A classic animated plasma made by a GPU shader, with a slider for its scale. Select the Shader node and edit the GLSL in the side panel.

samples.name: Shader · Feedback Ripples
samples.description: A shader that feeds on its own last frame: each frame blurs and fades the previous picture and adds a moving source, so ripples build up.

samples.name: Shader · Reaction-Diffusion
samples.description: Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion running on the GPU in several passes: each pass moves the chemicals one step on, and a final pass turns them into colour. Give it a few seconds to bloom.

samples.name: Fractal Tree
samples.description: A tree whose branching is worked out inside the patch, with no pre-drawn coordinates. A ForEach walks 8 paths from root to tip, four levels each, turning left or right at every fork and making each branch 0.7 times as long as the last. Change the turn, the shrink or the trunk length and the tree reshapes.

samples.name: Datamosh
samples.description: Load a picture and layer four tinted copies of it, drifting apart over time and blended together, for a colour-fringing glitch look.

samples.name: Photo Mosaic
samples.description: Reads a 32×32 grid of colours from a picture and draws each as a dot sized by its brightness: a pointillist look that breathes with time.

samples.name: Webcam Mosaic
samples.description: A live, mirrored webcam halftone. Switch the Toggle on and allow camera access; each cell becomes a yellow circle where the picture is light and a blue square where it is dark.

samples.name: Body Tracking
samples.description: A live skeleton from your webcam. One Toggle starts the camera and the tracker; cyan lines join the points and yellow dots mark them. Switch between hands, face and pose on the Landmarks node.

samples.name: Video Pixelate
samples.description: A looping video made chunky with Pixelate. Click Replace… on the VideoFile node to play your own MP4 or MOV, or wire a number from 0 to 1 into its scrub pin to move through the video.

samples.name: Pixel Sort
samples.description: Classic glitch art: runs of pixels along each row are sorted by brightness, but only inside a low-to-high brightness range. Drag the sliders to shift the streaks.

samples.name: Tone Surface
samples.description: Move the mouse — X picks pitch, Y picks amplitude. A 20×20 grid lights up around the cursor.

samples.name: FFT Bloom
samples.description: A tone is split into its spectrum and drawn as a ring: each of 64 frequency bands becomes a dot. The mouse’s height sets the pitch.

samples.name: Random Walk Trail
samples.description: A walker wanders in random directions, leaving a trail of 200 points. The colour cycles along the trail and the oldest points fade.

samples.name: Paint Trail
samples.description: Move the mouse to paint. Each stroke is kept on a hidden canvas that is fed back every frame, so the paint stays, and its colour cycles over time.

samples.name: Echo Trails
samples.description: Echo keeps the last frames on the GPU: a swinging star leaves ten fading copies. Try trails, delay, slit-scan, freeze.

samples.name: CSV Bar Chart
samples.description: Numbers typed into a CSVInline node become 16 coloured bars. Edit its data to chart a different series.

samples.name: Local Peaks
samples.description: Bars of noise where a bar lights up green only if it is taller than both of its neighbours: a simple way to find peaks.

samples.name: Number Counters
samples.description: Format Number: an eased count-up as money, percent and compact 12.3k, and a m:ss.ff clock.

samples.name: Voronoi Mosaic
samples.description: Evenly spread random points become Voronoi cells with gaps between them, filled from a palette, with their corners rounded off. A new seed gives a new mosaic.

samples.name: L-System Plant
samples.description: A plant grown by an L-system (a set of rewriting rules) repeated five times and drawn like a turtle walking. A little jitter makes it organic, and an LFO sways it.

samples.name: Contour Blobs
samples.description: Random circles merged into one blob, then grown and shrunk again and again to make rings like a contour map.

samples.name: Plexus
samples.description: Connect Points joins nearby boids with lines that fade and thin as they stretch, a few links per bird.

samples.name: Morph Tunnel
samples.description: Shape Morph blends a circle into a star. 22 copies, each shrinking and turning a little more, breathe from round to spiky.

samples.name: Relaxed Cells
samples.description: The same random points before and after Scatter's relax (Lloyd relaxation): clumps and gaps become an even mosaic.

samples.name: Loop Bloom
samples.description: A ring of dots breathing in a travelling wave, built on the Time node's loop phase so it repeats perfectly every 5 s — export one loop as MP4 or GIF (File → Export Video / GIF…) and it plays on repeat without a seam.

samples.name: Flocking
samples.description: Simulation in flocking mode: 300 boids separate, align and cohere on a wrapping field. Sliders reshape the flock live; the mouse herds it.

samples.name: Slime Mould
samples.description: Simulation in physarum mode: 20 000 agents lay and follow a trail map that grows into veins. The trail map is an image, coloured by a palette ramp; the mouse feeds it.

samples.name: DLA Coral
samples.description: Simulation in dla mode: random walkers stick to a growing cluster and it branches like coral. Lines join each particle to its parent, coloured by growth order.

samples.name: Cloth
samples.description: Simulation in cloth mode: a mesh of springs hung from two corners, blown by gusts. Drag it with the mouse; pull hard and it tears.

samples.name: Gradient Sunset
samples.description: Gradient fills and a mask: a linear sky, a sun graded across its own box, hard-edged repeating gradient stripes that slide down and mask the sun by luminance, and a turning conic-gradient ring.

samples.name: Neon Bloom
samples.description: Post-effects on the GPU: two counter-rotating neon polygons (conic gradient strokes) through a chain of Effect nodes — bloom, chromatic aberration, animated film grain and a vignette. Switch any Effect's mode to try displace, dither or halftone.

samples.name: Variations & Presets
samples.description: A seeded flow field of strokes. Vary (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+R) re-rolls the patch seed for a new picture; the Presets panel recalls Calm or Storm, or morphs between them.

samples.name: Rose Curve
samples.description: A rose of 900 dots from the Curve node: a slider sets the petals, an LFO turns them, a Linear spread of hues runs round the colour wheel along the curve and a Sine Spread ripples the dot sizes.

samples.name: Cellular Warp
samples.description: One Noise node paints a whole 64×64 grid at once: cellular noise with sharp cell walls, bent by a second noise field and drifting with time, coloured through a gradient. Switch its mode to perlin, simplex or value.

samples.name: Topographic
samples.description: Contours traces drifting noise on a grid at 14 levels: the lines of a topographic map, slowly shifting.

samples.name: Colour Spaces
samples.description: The same red → blue blend in RGB, OKLab and OKLCH (Lerp's space option), a cosine palette, and a tetradic harmony around a base colour whose hue turns with time (Palette's generator modes).

samples.name: Metaballs
samples.description: Gooey metaballs made with Effect nodes: blur the circles, then cut the blur at a level so nearby circles melt together, with a glow and an inner shadow for depth. Orbiting circles merge and split.

samples.name: Colour Grade
samples.description: Key out a green backdrop to put petals on a gradient sky (with spill suppression), then grade the colour with Levels, Curves (cool shadows, warm highlights) and a 3D LUT loaded from a .cube file.

samples.name: Rainy Night
samples.description: Lens blur turns scattered lights into bokeh discs, motion blur streaks falling rain along its angle, and barrel distortion bulges the frame like a wide lens.

samples.name: Warp Speed
samples.description: A starfield through spin blur (arcs round the centre) and zoom blur (streaks from it), the zoom pulsing with an LFO for a jump to hyperspace.

samples.name: Marble, Wood & Op Art
samples.description: Noise's pattern modes, domain-warped: stripes → marble, rings → wood grain, checker → op art. The panels go through blur, posterize and edges for a topographic map.

samples.name: Path Ops Shapes
samples.description: Six Path Ops modes: round corners, thicken (a spiral stroke outlined), wave, noise and twist deformers (phases looping with Time), and explode (a hexagon's edges pushed apart).

samples.name: Flipbook Sequence
samples.description: Video plays image sequences too: 16 PNG frames of a flower, carried inside the patch, loop at 12 fps, onion-skinned by Echo. Pick one frame of your own numbered run (Floret's PNG-sequence export, say) to play the lot.

samples.name: Layout Bloom
samples.description: Layout arranges a sunflower spiral whose count steps every 1.8 s: the seeds ease to their new places, new ones grow in and the extra ones shrink away, staggered from the centre out.

samples.name: Point Tracker
samples.description: Point Tracker follows three points across a drifting field of dots, frame by frame, from the picture alone. Each marker’s colour shows how sure it is, and Echo trails show the paths.

samples.name: Plexus Colours
samples.description: Connect Points colours each line from its two birds: every boid takes a hue from where it flies, and a line blends from one end's colour to the other's.

samples.name: Topo Type
samples.description: The Contours node in shape mode: rings at even distances round a word, filled like the bands of a contour map, each level its own colour from a palette.

samples.name: Stippled Sphere
samples.description: The Scatter node’s stipple mode shades a lit sphere and its shadow with 2600 ink dots: they gather where the picture is dark and relax into an even, hand-stippled grain.

samples.name: Time Smear
samples.description: A Shader with history switched on reads the input’s past frames: each band of the picture shows a spinning star as it was a different moment ago, a rolling datamosh time smear.

samples.name: Neon Orbits
samples.description: Effect’s glow in add blend mode: three neon orbits cross over a dark grid, and where their halos overlap the light adds up instead of covering what’s beneath.

samples.name: Camera Slit-Scan
samples.description: The webcam through Echo's slit-scan: each row of the picture comes from a moment further back, so anything that moves stretches and bends. Without a camera, a swinging stand-in shows the effect.

samples.name: Flow Lines
samples.description: Contours' flow mode: evenly spaced streamlines through a noise field, each line a colour from the palette — the plotter-art look, slowly turning with time.

samples.name: Mondrian Splits
samples.description: Cells' subdivide mode: a square split recursively by chance, black gaps between the parts, colours picked at random from a mostly-white palette.

samples.name: Truchet Tiles
samples.description: The Tiles node's truchet mode: quarter-circle tiles turned by noise, so the arcs clump into long meandering loops in two colours.

samples.name: WFC Circuits
samples.description: The Tiles node's wfc mode: wave function collapse over edge-matched pipe tiles, none running off the grid, each tile type in its own colour.

samples.name: Kaleido Slime
samples.description: The Symmetry node's kaleidoscope mode: a slime mould's trail map cut to a wedge and mirrored six times round the centre, a growing lace mandala.

samples.name: Wallpaper Groups
samples.description: The Symmetry node’s wallpaper mode: a small turning motif repeated across a hexagonal lattice. Pick any of the 17 wallpaper groups.

samples.name: Differential Growth
samples.description: The Simulation node's growth mode: a ring whose nodes repel and whose edges split as they stretch, folding like coral; edges coloured by age.

samples.name: Reaction Diffusion
samples.description: The Simulation node's reaction mode: Gray–Scott coral growing out of a rasterised word, with presets for mitosis, fingerprints, worms and more.

samples.name: ASCII Cells
samples.description: The Effect node's ascii mode: reaction–diffusion fingerprint ridges redrawn as coloured characters picked by brightness.

samples.name: Palette From Image
samples.description: The Palette node’s image mode: a photo’s six dominant colours, used to colour a Mondrian beside it.

samples.name: Ecosystem
samples.description: Boids graze on food that regrows: each steers for its nearest ripe item (Simulation’s food pin), meals grow the population and hunger thins it, boom and bust in a live chart. Hold the mouse to grow food; sliders for hunger, speed, regrowth, metabolism.

samples.name: Epidemic (SIR)
samples.description: 320 wanderers, susceptible, then infected, then recovered: each catches it from the nearest infected person within a radius. Click to infect; sliders for radius, roaming, recovery, waning immunity; lockdown toggle; presets; live chart.

samples.name: Orbital Sandbox
samples.description: Bodies orbiting a binary star, their positions and speeds remembered between frames by Read and Write pairs. Drag and release to slingshot new bodies in; time-warp and star-separation sliders; Echo trails.

samples.name: Weather Map
samples.description: A drifting pressure field drawn as filled bands and isobars (Contours), with geostrophic wind feeding flow lines, 320 advected particles and a grid of arrows; H and L at the extremes. XY pad moves the storm; sliders for its depth and the wind.

samples.name: Living Clock
samples.description: The real time as a picture (the Clock node): second ticks, minute and hour arcs, the year's days on a spiral, the Moon's actual phase and the date spelled out, over a sky that follows the hour. Time-travel slider, 12/24-hour toggle.

samples.name: Topographic Reaction
samples.description: Reaction–diffusion you paint with the mouse, read as terrain by Contours (filled elevation bands and isolines) and printed on grainy paper. Presets switch the chemistry; a toggle shows the raw chemicals.

samples.name: Plotter Pipeline
samples.description: Flow-field streamlines in three inks, drawn line after line by Trim Path with a pen riding the tip, on paper with a shadow and grain. Sliders for pen width, spacing, field scale and plot speed; Replot; a clean-output toggle for export.

samples.name: Parallax Valley
samples.description: Five noise ridges sliding past at parallax speeds, fading into the sky by distance, with fog bands, a sun and moon on an arc, stars at night and a small flock of birds. Time-of-day and travel sliders; move the mouse to look around.

samples.name: Night City
samples.description: A city from one subdivision: per-block heights, roofs and sun shadows in a ForEach, windows scattered on the roofs, cars as Trim Path pieces circling the blocks and lamps along the streets, blooming after dark. Time-of-day and density sliders; Vary.

samples.name: Seasons Garden
samples.description: L-system plants that grow (Trim Path), sway in the wind and turn with the seasons; autumn leaves and winter snow fall from particle emitters in a windy world. Season and wind sliders, auto-year toggle, Replant.

samples.name: Tile World
samples.description: An island from noise elevation (coloured Cells), wave-function-collapse roads masked to land, Symmetry rosettes for forests and villages, drifting metaball clouds with shadows and a day/night cycle with village lights. Sea-level and time sliders; Vary.

samples.name: Data Story
samples.description: An animated bar-chart race from inline CSV: each year’s numbers are ranked, the bars ease into place, a line revealed by Trim Path traces the yearly totals, and captions animate in. Play toggle, year stepper, speed slider.

samples.name: Generative Band
samples.description: A self-playing trio — noise-walk melody (MonoSynth, delay, reverb), sawtooth bass, noise hats — and the same numbers drawn: a 16-step ring, note bursts, the melody's spectrum and waveform, through trails and bloom. Sliders for bpm, density, volume; major/minor.

samples.name: Glitch Tracker
samples.description: Generated footage tracked by optical flow (Point Tracker) with a HUD of boxes and links, while the picture goes through Echo slit-scan, chromatic aberration and displacement bursts. Hold the mouse to re-seed the trackers; glitch slider; slit-scan toggle.

samples.name: Generative Poster
samples.description: A Swiss-style poster as rules: Layout grid modules picking shapes, turns and harmony colours from seeded noise, an animated title and a grain or halftone finish. Colour picker, columns slider (modules ease to the new grid), Vary, and presets to morph between.

samples.name: Brush Studio
samples.description: Paint with the mouse on a canvas fed back to itself: keys 1–4 switch ink, ribbon, spray and rainbow brushes, M mirrors every stroke eight ways, C clears.

samples.name: Slingshot Sandbox
samples.description: Press, pull back and let go to fling balls round bumpers, with an aiming arc; G cycles gravity, W bouncing or wrapping walls, C clears, R rain.

samples.name: Flock Herder
samples.description: Hold the mouse to lure a flock of boids (F turns the lure into a scare); keys 1–3 change its character, S scatters it. Plexus lines and trails.

samples.name: Breakout
samples.description: A complete game from nodes: the paddle follows the mouse, click to launch, bricks break into sparks, score, lives and levels. Plays itself until you click.

samples.name: Voronoi Editor
samples.description: Drag points to reshape Voronoi cells, click to add, X to remove, hold L to relax them; D shows the Delaunay triangles, H the hull. The nearest point to the mouse is found with Lookup and Statistics.

samples.name: Typing Toy
samples.description: Type and each letter drops in with a bounce, a spin and sparks, then bobs on a wave under a rainbow; Keyboard's text mode keeps the string.

samples.name: Kaleidoscope Toy
samples.description: Beads tumble in a round chamber seen through mirrors: drag sideways to turn the tube (gravity turns too) and drop beads; keys 3–9 set the mirrors.

samples.name: Reaction Painter
samples.description: Drag to paint chemical into a live reaction–diffusion dish; keys 1–7 switch coral, mitosis, fingerprints, worms, maze, spots and waves while it runs.

samples.name: MIDI Garden
samples.description: Every MIDI note plants a flower and plays it; CC knobs turn hue, petals, spin and bloom. No MIDI: sliders, keys A–K and clicks stand in.

samples.name: Preset Morph
samples.description: A spirograph to perform: six presets to recall or morph between in the Presets panel, Vary for new phases, the XY pad and a drag to fan the layers.

samples.name: Step Sequencer
samples.description: A 16 × 8 tone matrix: click or drag cells, the playhead plays each lit column through four MonoSynth voices, Mix, filter, delay and reverb. Tempo, tone, scale.

samples.name: Keyboard Synth
samples.description: Play the computer keyboard like a piano (A–K, W E T Y U), Z / X for octaves, mouse for the filter, and an arpeggiator for held chords; sparks and a scope.

samples.name: Hand Theremin
samples.description: Raise a hand to the webcam (or hold the mouse): left–right is pitch, snapped to a scale or gliding, up–down is loudness; rings and a string vibrate with it.

samples.name: Mic Bloom
samples.description: A flower that listens: the microphone's spectrum becomes its petals, bass swells the core, beats send rings out. Plays its own demo loop until the mic is on.

samples.name: Music Box
samples.description: Pins on a turning disc pluck a comb: a noise-composed tune in a scale, three bell voices. Click the disc to add or remove pins, N for a new tune.

samples.name: Hand Sparks
samples.description: Wave your hands at the camera and they throw sparks: the faster they move, the more fly. A Write/Read pair remembers last frame's hand points, so the patch can measure how far each moved and turn that speed into an emit rate. One Toggle starts the camera and the hand tracker.

samples.name: Camera Embers
samples.description: You, made of rising embers: the live camera's bright areas gather points (Scatter in stipple mode), and each point sheds glowing sparks that drift up on turbulence. No camera or permission yet? A swaying stand-in glow sheds embers instead.
